NPR Check These Out Microsoft's Office Scripts sample gallery — a browsable library of working scripts rather than API documentation. The quick scenarios are the useful part for workpapers: copy multiple tables into one table, generate a workbook table of contents, count blank rows across every sheet, output a range as JSON, save and email a sheet as PDF. Each ships with a downloadable workbook, so you can watch one run against real data before adapting it. Nothing to install — Office Scripts lives in the Automate tab of Excel on the web. GAO's Yellow Book page, worth a re-read for the 2024 edition dates — the 2024 revision takes effect for financial audits of periods beginning on or after December 15, 2025, and separately requires a compliant system of quality management to be designed and implemented by December 15, 2025 with the first evaluation completed by December 15, 2026. That evaluation deadline is the one that sneaks up on small firms, and it is a firm-level obligation rather than an engagement-level one. Tips Excel: get back to where you were with Ctrl+Backspace. When you have scrolled somewhere far from the active cell — which happens constantly in a 364-account trial balance — Ctrl+Backspace scrolls the window straight back so the active cell is visible again, without moving the selection. It is the counterpart to Ctrl+G, which moves the selection; this one moves only the view. Pair it with Ctrl+End to find the true last used cell when a workbook has phantom rows past the data. AutoHotkey v2: paste as plain text anywhere. Pasting from a PDF or a client email drags fonts, colors and highlighting into your workpaper. This strips it everywhere, including apps that ignore Ctrl+Shift+V: ^+v:: { saved := ClipboardAll() A_Clipboard := A_Clipboard ; drops all formatting Send "^v" Sleep 150 A_Clipboard := saved ; restore the original } Save it in your v2 script, reload, and Ctrl+Shift+V pastes clean text system-wide. The A_Clipboard := A_Clipboard line is the whole trick — reassigning the clipboard to itself keeps only the text.

Check These Out GASB 103 — what actually changes on the page Effective for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025, so it lands on June 30 year-ends now and works its way toward the September-30 governments after. The interesting part for anyone who has just spent a week inside an MD&A: it kills “extraordinary” and “special” items, mandates five specific MD&A sections written as analysis rather than boilerplate, and requires dual variance reporting in the budgetary comparison — original-to-final and final-to-actual, with explanations for the significant ones. xypha’s AHK v2 script collection A single showcase script plus standalone pieces, all written for v2 rather than ported from v1. Worth a browse for the text-case converter (lower / UPPER / Sentence / Title / INVERT on selected text), the pixel-by-pixel numpad mouse nudge for clicking tiny spreadsheet targets, and MultiClip — a 25-slot clipboard manager that persists across restarts, which is a different animal from Win+V. Tips Excel’s Inquire add-in will diff two workbooks cell by cell Useful when a review round hands you a “same file, few changes” pair — exactly the 25d situation. Turn it on once at File › Options › Add-ins, choose COM Add-ins in the Manage box, Go, then tick Inquire. An Inquire tab appears; open both workbooks and hit Compare Files. It reports changed values, changed formulas, and changed formatting in separate colours, which finds a moved rounding plug faster than eyes do. It ships with Office Professional Plus and Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise. Chrome’s address bar can search a single site Visit a site with a search box once — Drive, Todoist, the GASB site — and Chrome usually records its search engine. After that, type enough of the domain to match, press Tab, and the omnibox switches to searching inside that site only. If a site did not register, add it by hand at chrome://settings/searchEngines with a short keyword and a URL containing %s . Two keystrokes replaces loading a page and then finding its search field.

Tips Excel finds row-level mismatches with one keystroke Select two adjacent columns you are tying out — a client figure beside yours — and press Ctrl+\ (Go To Special, Row differences). Excel selects only the cells in each row that differ from the leftmost column, so a fill color applied right after leaves every break highlighted and everything that ties untouched. Ctrl+Shift+\ does the same across columns. Chrome can search a site straight from the address bar Type the start of a site you use often, such as drive.google.com, then press Tab — the bar switches to searching inside that site and your next keystrokes go to its own search.
